headline: No reason given: Amanpour leaves CNN after 43 years.
summary: Christiane Amanpour, CNN's chief international anchor, said Monday she will leave the network in June 2027. Her nightly CNN International show goes weekly in January and ends in May. Her PBS show ends this year. She gave no reason. The exit comes two weeks after Skydance closed its $81 billion buyout of CNN's parent.

cover_question.q: Why leave if she's so good at it?

cover_answer: No reason given. At 68, she set her own leaving date.
table_question: When is the right time to stop doing something you're good at?

5-7.chip: Bring it up if it fits the day
5-7.script: Christiane Amanpour has told people the news on TV for 43 years, longer than most of your teachers have been alive. She flew to places where wars were happening and told everyone far away what she saw. Next year she will stop and try new things. She chose it herself, and she is fine.
5-7.why: The job as a picture: flying off to look, then telling. A six-year-old needs to hear she is fine, so the script ends there.
5-7.why_long: A six-year-old reasons from what is in front of them, so the job becomes a picture: flying to where the trouble is and telling everyone far away. Leaving a job can sound like being sent away, so the script says she chose, and that she is fine. Expect "did she get in trouble?" No. She decided. Her boss said thank you.

8-12.script: In 1983 one of Amanpour's bosses told her she didn't have what it took to be a foreign correspondent. She became CNN's best-known war reporter anyway, from the Gulf War to Ukraine. At 68 she has set her own leaving date, June 2027. One wrong call, then a scoreboard 43 years long.
8-12.why: A wrong boss and a long scoreboard. Kids this age keep score.
8-12.why_long: This age is working out whether adults judge fairly, so the script hands them a chain to check: one boss said no, the record said otherwise for 43 years. The scoreboard is the mechanism, evidence outlasting an opinion. Expect "why leave if she's so good?" She didn't say. Her boss says it is the right time.

13-17.script: Amanpour's rule is "always be truthful, not neutral." Can a reporter be both, or does one give? Second: she gave no reason, and the news came two weeks after an $81 billion merger gave CNN a new owner. Coincidence, or the reason she didn't say?
13-17.why: Her own rule, then the timing. Follow the evidence with them.
13-17.why_long: A teenager can hold two true things at once: Amanpour gave no reason, and the timing sits two weeks after the merger. The script asks them to argue from those two facts without inventing a third, and to notice when they want to. Expect "so was she pushed?" Nobody has said so. Say that plainly and leave the gap open.

5-7.q: Why is she leaving her job?
5-7.a: She didn't say why. After 43 years she wants to try new projects. Her boss said thank you and that everyone will be sad to see her go.

8-12.q: Why leave if she's so good at it?
8-12.a: She didn't say. Her boss says they talked for months and it's the right time.

8-12.q: What does a chief international anchor do?
8-12.a: Reports news from other countries and runs her own interview show.

13-17.q: Did the merger push her out?
13-17.a: Nobody has said so. She gave no reason. The timing is all anyone has.
Report what the evidence shows, even when it favours one side.
